page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top ("AD INDOS."), page number "II" at the top right. No notes in the margins, no footnotes, no catchword at the foot. The text ends with the hyphenated word "Annun-", which continues on the next page.

main_text.p: id inter omnia quæ ad cultum fuum requirit urget præcipuè ; quod etiam primum nobis in precibus esse jussit : quocirca & necessitatum hujus vitæ curam, donorum item animæ necessariorum postulationem, hac sollicitudine atque hoc officio posteriorem instituit : Æquum enim est nihil creaturæ prius esse, curâ honoris & gloriæ creatori suo debitæ : nihil ipsi enixius totis viribus contendendum, quàm ut Deus ab hominibus, quos ad cultum suum formavit, eâ quâ decet reverentiâ & religione colatur : ut ei omnes vivant, qui omnibus vitam dedit : ei quisque serviat, qui suis servitutem peccati & mortis excussit. Rex ille Regum mundi, licet in Sacris suis literis hac de re plane sileret, neque nostram so-cordiam, crebris promissionum stimulis in-citaret, generosi tamen militis officium requirit, ne Domino absente imperium ab hoste invasum, prædæ & libidini adversariorum exponat, aut semel occupatum pa-cificè possideri patiatur : jam verò quale hoc nostrum debet esse studium, quum lucri & incrementi summopere avidus, damni ultra modum impatiens, à nobis, ut servis frugi, rem suam familiarem, minis additis, augeri jubeat : regni limi-tes protendi, passim in suis scriptis postulet. Annun-

page.notes: A small mark stands after "postulet." (possibly a reference or printer's mark); it is not transcribed. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, e.g. "esse", "jussit", "suis", "studium". The word "debitæ" is followed by a colon with no space in print ("debitæ :nihil"); it is transcribed with a space. Printed "cordiam,crebris" and "cificè" run together at the line ends; the hyphenated forms are kept as printed.
